free_tier.stated: A global gateway to a DDoS-protected developer platform with public domains for localhost.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is published on the front page.; ingress: tcp

interface_detail: Download the Connect plugin or run the Gate connector; a dashboard at app.minekube.com issues the public domain.
tooling: Connect plugin or the Gate connector on the origin
chaining: Gives a localhost Minecraft server a public hostname over an outbound connection, so it composes with a free VM that has no inbound ports.

limits.value: reaching the network requires running a connector (plugin or Gate) on the origin

binding_note: Minekube Connect is a TCP edge for Minecraft, so the UDP test fails before any quota is reached.

identity_cost.detail: An account on app.minekube.com, plus a connector plugin or the Gate agent on the origin. The register form was not read.

reliability_note: Traffic passes a shared superproxy; the origin runs a connector that holds the connection open.
confidence_note: The vendor's own words describe a TCP edge. A Bedrock path, if one exists behind the connector, would change the record and would need its docs pages read.

evidence.proved: Minekube Connect is described as 'a cloud-native Minecraft TCP edge network' giving public domains for localhost, reached by a self-hosted Connector

notes: Included because the name circulates in free Minecraft proxy lists. It is TCP by design and therefore out's UDP test, but it is the one candidate that solves the private-origin problem, which TCPShield's tunnel also solves.

extras.wg_detail: A Minecraft TCP edge network; no UDP ingress is described.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published on the front page.
extras.transit_note: Minekube's superproxy carries the game traffic
